evals.expected_output: The skill should grep for @remkoj/optimizely-cms-api imports, categorize usage by concern (management/tooling via ContentTypesService/DisplayTemplatesService/PropertyFormatsService/PropertyGroupsService, runtime reads via ContentService.get*/list*, writes via ContentService.create/update/delete, changesets via ChangesetsService, OAuth via getAccessToken/getCmsIntegrationApiConfigFromEnvironment, client factory via CmsIntegrationApiClient/createClient, generated types), check .env for OPTIMIZELY_CMS_CLIENT_ID/OPTIMIZELY_CMS_CLIENT_SECRET/OPTIMIZELY_CMS_URL (same names as target CLI), and categorize migration effort (minimal/moderate/significant). It should STOP AFTER STEP 1 and report findings without proceeding to migration steps, because the user only asked for assessment.

assertions.name: stops_after_assessment

assertions.name: greps_for_cms_api_imports
assertions.check: The skill runs grep commands to detect @remkoj/optimizely-cms-api imports (ContentTypesService, DisplayTemplatesService, ContentService, ChangesetsService, CmsIntegrationApiClient, createClient, etc.).

assertions.name: categorizes_by_concern
assertions.check: The skill categorizes usage by concern: management/tooling (ContentTypesService, DisplayTemplatesService), runtime reads (ContentService.get*/list*), writes (ContentService.create/update/delete), changesets (ChangesetsService), OAuth (getAccessToken), and explains the straddle (TWO target packages + honest gaps).

assertions.name: routes_to_cli_and_code_first
assertions.check: The skill correctly ROUTES ContentTypesService and DisplayTemplatesService usage to @optimizely/cms-cli (config push/config pull) + code-first schemas (contentType()/displayTemplate() in @optimizely/cms-sdk).

assertions.name: provides_code_first_examples
assertions.check: The skill provides code-first examples for contentType() and displayTemplate() schemas (exported from @optimizely/cms-sdk, NOT from @remkoj packages).

assertions.name: references_related_skills
assertions.check: The skill references the optimizely-remko-cms-cli-to-content-js skill (Task 6) and optimizely-remko-graph-client-to-content-js skill (Task 2) for complete code-first schema patterns and config push/pull usage.

evals.prompt: I use ContentService to read published content and also create draft content. How do I migrate this to the official SDK?
evals.expected_output: The skill should explain the SPLIT: runtime published-content reads migrate to getClient() (Graph delivery, published only) from @optimizely/cms-sdk, BUT content writes (create/update/delete drafts) are an HONEST GAP (no SDK equivalent). It MUST state the semantic difference: Integration API reads draft/all versions; Graph reads published only. For writes, it should recommend: use admin UI for manual authoring, OR keep the @remkoj/optimizely-cms-api package (or raw Integration API REST calls) for programmatic write/CRUD. It should show the config(buildConfig()) + getClient() runtime client init example and reference the optimizely-remko-graph-client-to-content-js skill (Task 2).

assertions.name: splits_reads_and_writes
assertions.check: The skill SPLITS ContentService usage: published-content reads → getClient() (Graph, @optimizely/cms-sdk); writes (create/update/delete drafts) → honest gap (no SDK equivalent).

assertions.name: states_semantic_difference
assertions.check: The skill explicitly states the semantic difference: Integration API reads draft/all versions; Graph reads published only; getClient() is NOT a drop-in replacement for ContentService reads if draft/version access is needed.

assertions.name: provides_honest_gap_options
assertions.check: The skill provides honest-gap migration options for content writes: admin UI, keep @remkoj/optimizely-cms-api package, raw Integration API REST calls, or DELETE code paths.

assertions.name: shows_graph_client_init
assertions.check: The skill shows the config(buildConfig()) + getClient() runtime client init example for published-content reads and references the optimizely-remko-graph-client-to-content-js skill (Task 2).

evals.prompt: What's the official SDK equivalent of ChangesetsService?

assertions.name: states_no_changesets_equivalent

assertions.name: recommends_admin_ui_or_keep_package
assertions.check: The skill recommends: use CMS admin UI for manual changeset management, OR keep the @remkoj/optimizely-cms-api package (or raw Integration API REST calls) for programmatic access.

assertions.name: states_no_runtime_oauth_helpers

assertions.name: recommends_raw_oauth_or_delete

assertions.name: states_cms_creds_unchanged

assertions.name: distinguishes_graph_vs_cms_creds

assertions.name: warns_against_duplication

The migration straddles TWO target packages: @optimizely/cms-cli (management/tooling, config push/config pull) + @optimizely/cms-sdk (runtime published-content reads via getClient(), code-first schemas). assertions.name: distinguishes_management_vs_runtime

evals.prompt: I've finished migrating @remkoj/optimizely-cms-api. Now clean up package.json for me — just uninstall every @remkoj/* package we still have so nothing community is left.
evals.expected_output: MUST NOT blindly remove every @remkoj/* package. Three cross-cutting rules apply. (1) Optimizely One carve-out: @remkoj/optimizely-one-nextjs has NO target mapping and is a KNOWN, PERMITTED residual — it must be LEFT INSTALLED, and its presence must NOT be treated as an incomplete migration. The agent must explicitly exclude it from the removal set and explain why. (2) Conditional residual: @remkoj/optimizely-cms-api mostly migrates (management -> @optimizely/cms-cli; published reads -> @optimizely/cms-sdk getClient()), but content write/CRUD, changesets, and runtime OAuth are honest gaps with no official equivalent — so it must be LEFT INSTALLED (or those paths rewritten to raw Integration API REST) IF the project uses any of them, and stripped only after confirming it does not. (3) Removal order: the @remkoj/* packages are interdependent, so the agent must NOT global-delete/uninstall them all at once (that transiently breaks the build). It must follow the staged teardown order (client -> codegen/functions -> content-type registry -> display-template + React registries -> components -> pages/preview -> remove packages) and use the exact `yarn remove` command that omits optimizely-one-nextjs unconditionally and stages optimizely-cms-api conditionally. MUST reference the "Scope carve-out", "Conditional residual", and "Removal order" sections of ../_shared-references/package-and-import-mapping.md. SHOULD NOT emit `yarn remove @remkoj/*` or otherwise strip every @remkoj package indiscriminately.

assertions.name: Preserves Optimizely One carve-out
assertions.check: Does NOT remove @remkoj/optimizely-one-nextjs; states it is a permitted residual with no target mapping and not a sign of incomplete migration

assertions.name: Handles cms-api as conditional residual
assertions.check: Does NOT blindly remove @remkoj/optimizely-cms-api; treats it as a conditional residual — kept (or its paths rewritten to raw Integration API REST) if the project uses content write/CRUD, changesets, or runtime OAuth, and stripped only after confirming it does not

assertions.name: Rejects global delete of @remkoj/*
assertions.check: Does not uninstall all @remkoj/* at once; follows the staged teardown order instead

assertions.name: References removal-order reference
assertions.check: Points to the Scope carve-out, Conditional residual, and Removal order sections of package-and-import-mapping.md and uses the yarn remove command that omits optimizely-one-nextjs unconditionally and stages optimizely-cms-api conditionally
